Priya Nair: Heads-up: benchmark results for the percentile-aware priority queue + adaptive backpressure feature are in. Big wins on bursty traffic. p50 -2%, p95 -12%, p99 -30% for our conversational burst suite. cost per 1k tokens -6%.
Liam O'Connor: hell yeah. which test harness did BenchBot run? full-prod trace replay or synthetic bursts?
BenchBot: ran replay of 72h traffic sample (region: us-west-2) + additional synthetic spike tests at 3x inbound rate.
Evelyn Park: can you drop the key graphs? want to see breakdown by seq length and model family.
Priya Nair: snapshots: https://dash.redwood.internal/bench/2071122334 and summary table: p99 wins concentrated on sessions with >400 tokens and on models with long KV caches. Short single-turn requests show negligible change.
Liam O'Connor: what's the config we tested?
Priya Nair: config snippet:
```
priority_queue_v1:
  window_ms: 250
  priority_decay: 0.85
  percentile_target: 99
backpressure:
  enabled: true
  scale_factor: 1.4
  probe_rate_ms: 500
```
Evelyn Park: noticed a slight increase in CPU on host due to queueing logic?
sre-bot: host-cpu +3% on canary nodes, GPU utilization stable. memory unchanged. error-rate unchanged.
Liam O'Connor: any impact on tail token-cost accounting?
Priya Nair: token-cost down ~6% across the canary slice; cost per inference improved because batching efficiency rose during spikes.
BenchBot: quality checks: 0 failures on automated eval sets; no regression on hallucination or truncation.
Priya Nair: deploy-bot started canary at 2071122340 -> rollout 7%.
deploy-bot: Canary snapshot @+30m: p99 -28% vs baseline, cost -5.8%, user-latency p50 similar. Link: https://sre.redwood.internal/snapshots/2071122334-30m
Liam O'Connor: flag: small-prompt 1-5 token requests saw p10 degrade by ~6ms in synthetic microbench. Might be due to extra queue mgmt checks.
Evelyn Park: let's add a fast-path for tiny requests (<=8 tokens) in priority queue to avoid perf cliff.
Priya Nair: agreed. we'll gate the fast-path via model-tag and add a config toggle: tiny_fast_path: true (default off during canary).
Liam O'Connor: rollback condition?
Priya Nair: auto-rollback if p99 increases > 8% or error-rate +0.7% absolute for 10m. Manual rollback cmd in runbook.
Evelyn Park: I'll add a short RFC and update the runtime runbook with the new knobs.
Docs: I'll prep a short internal note and DevEx guide showing when to enable priority queue or fast-paths (chat vs rpc).
Priya Nair: plan: hold at 7% for 1h, then 25% if stable, flip tiny_fast_path on for short-tagged models, then continue to 100% roll in 6h if no regressions. I'll post status updates here.
Liam O'Connor: great. any immediate customer-facing risk?
Priya Nair: none observed in canary. SRE will monitor for 72h and page on the usual SLO alerts.
Evelyn Park: action items: (1) add tiny_fast_path gate PR, (2) docs update, (3) runbook rollback commands. I'll own (1) and (3).
Priya Nair: TL;DR: percentile-aware priority queue + adaptive backpressure reduces tail latency a lot for bursty long-chat traffic (p99 ~30% lower) and lowers token cost ~6%. Canary rolling now. :rocket:
